change.title: Lead the welcome screen with the video invitation, not the 'your code is on its way, go check your email' notice
change.targets: In-app entry (index.html welcome screen), claim-forwarded users: arrived -> pick a role -> reach the create screen
change.expected_effect: A few points of extra arrived->role among claim-forwarded users, flowing downstream to a few more finished videos and thus more in-app thank-you review clicks (the 89% engine). Directionally positive; below the noise floor at this traffic.
change.why_it_helps: Right now the first and loudest thing a person sees after they land in the create app is 'your code is on its way - go check your email', which tells them the reason they scanned is handled and points them straight out to their inbox. Leading instead with the invitation to make a video gives an undecided visitor a reason to stay and start one, which is what eventually earns a review.
changes_in_plain_words: The welcome screen now opens with the video invitation ('Turn your gift into a video they'll love') as the biggest, first thing you see - instead of a big green 'your 30% off code is on its way'.
The 'your code is on its way' message is kept, but shrunk to one calm line underneath, still showing the exact email address it was sent to.

The 'Not in your inbox? Check your spam folder.' line and the 'While you wait...' label were removed from this screen (the spam reminder still appears later on the 'Check your email' screen, where it's actually useful).

previews.label: the welcome screen a person sees right after they land in the create app (coming from the claim page)

change.why_the_rate_is_what_it_is: This step is NOT an exchange - these users have already paid the price (submitted their email, received the discount promise) and were auto-forwarded in. There is nothing left for them to 'give up'; the only question is motivation to spend a minute on an unannounced bonus. So the rate is a pure motivation/attention outcome, and the current screen spends its most valuable real estate (first paint, top, loudest) telling them the thing they came for is handled and pointing them away - actively lowering the motivation it should be raising.
what_would_have_to_be_true: A non-trivial share of the fast silent exiters are responding to the 'you're done / go check email' signal rather than being pure video-ceiling (unprovable at this traffic; the bet).
The create invitation, when it is the first/loudest element, is compelling enough to earn a role tap from an undecided arrival.

Demoting (not removing) the code confirmation does not break the discount promise - satisfied because a slim confirmation line is retained and the spam reassurance still appears on the final 'Check your email' screen where it's actually needed.
change.second_order_effects: Downstream review machinery is untouched: email is already captured on claim.html BEFORE this screen, the code is still sent by Klaviyo, and the video is still delivered by email - so nothing that feeds the review-reminder path changes (measured: phase=email_redirect review clicks = 0 in both 14d windows and 0 over 30d, so there is no email-reminder review volume to put at risk here anyway). One step further: the only plausible harm is a user who ONLY wanted the discount being momentarily less reassured their code is coming - mitigated by keeping an explicit one-line 'code on its way to {email}' confirmation and by the unchanged spam note on the final screen. If MORE warm users stay and finish videos, that increases load on the in-app thank-you review ask (the 89% engine) - the intended effect.
change.strongest_case_against: A sceptic would say: 'You proved people leave in <=6s with zero interaction - that is the signature of someone who never wanted the video, a ceiling. Reordering a header will not create desire that isn't there, and claim users already convert BETTER (63%) than non-claim (44%), so the block clearly isn't the problem. This is presentation polish dressed up as a fix, and at ~60 arrivals/fortnight you can never prove it either way.' My honest answer: I concede the cause is a bet and cannot be proven at this traffic (measurable:false, and I will never claim it worked without a SIGNIFICANT result). But the sceptic's own evidence - a decision made at first paint - is precisely why the first-paint content matters: if the loudest first thing is 'you're done, go check your email,' you are converting undecided arrivals into leavers at the exact instant they decide. The 63%>44% gap is confounded by intent (claim users are warmer, and the gap is itself non-significant, p=0.071) and shows only that the block is not catastrophic, not that it is optimal. The fix is cheap, reversible, on-brand, breaks no promise, and is asymmetric (cannot lower role-selection), so it is exactly the small compounding bet this job exists to make - and it is the structural in-app-entry KIND of change that historically moved this funnel (+14pts, 2026-06-16), not the claim-page reshuffle KIND that went flat.

tradeoff.gained: Removes a self-inflicted competing exit CTA at the highest-value warm-user drop; leads with a reason to stay and create, feeding the dominant (89%) review engine.
tradeoff.risked: Slightly less prominence on the 'your code is coming / check spam' reassurance for a user who only wanted the discount - mitigated by retaining a one-line code confirmation and by the unchanged spam reassurance on the final 'Check your email' screen. Downstream review-reminder volume is not at risk: email is captured upstream and phase=email_redirect review clicks = 0 in both 14d windows and 0 over 30d.
unverified_assumptions: Whether the fast <=6s silent exiters are responding to the done-signal vs a pure video-interest ceiling cannot be separated with current instruments (no micro-events between paint and role-select).

change.differs_from_past_attempt: The only prior in-app-entry attempt (2026-06-16) ADDED a value-prop text hero + a 'Free / Takes a minute / No app needed' cost line ABOVE the role cards - it never touched the code-status/'check your spam'/'while you wait' block that competes with the ask (in fact that hero copy currently sits BELOW the loud code block for claim users). This change re-ranks the hierarchy so the invitation leads and demotes/removes the competing inbox-exit CTA - a structural change to the same screen, distinct mechanism. It is on index.html, unrelated to the claim-page 07-23 imagery/voice work and to PR #8's claim-page reshuffle. It touches neither owner rejection: no discount code is handed over before the email (email was already given upstream), and it never references the printed percentage.

Booted the app (export .env vars, PORT=3939 node server.js in background) and fetched index.html?sku=PTT-GREEN1&from=claim&branch=receiver&email=test@example.com -> HTTP 200; asserted in the response that the invitation leads, the value line reads 'Free · Takes a minute · No app needed', the slim 'Your 30% off code is on its way to test@example.com' confirmation is present, and that 'YOUR 30% OFF CODE IS ON ITS WAY', 'Not in your inbox? Check your spam folder.' and 'While you wait...' are all gone from the arrival header, while the final Check-your-email screen still carries the spam note. Rendered mobile 390x844 full-page PNGs: AFTER from localhost (cycle-artifacts/2026-08-01/welcome-after.png) and BEFORE from the live site (welcome-before.png) - the AFTER reads premium/warm with the invitation as the clear hero and one calm code line; the BEFORE shows the old green code banner + spam CTA + 'WHILE YOU WAIT...' above the invitation, confirming the exact block being demoted. change.commit_message: feat(welcome): lead claim-arrival welcome with the create invitation, demote code-status to one calm line

pr_body:
## What this does

When someone lands in the create app after scanning the box and giving their email, the very first thing on the welcome screen was a big green **"YOUR 30% OFF CODE IS ON ITS WAY"**, then **"We sent your code to {email}"**, then **"Not in your inbox? Check your spam folder."** (a literal instruction to switch to their email app), then a **"While you wait..."** label - all *above* the invitation to make a video. In other words, the loudest first thing told a fast-glancing visitor "you're done, go check your inbox."

This change re-ranks that welcome header for these visitors:
- The video invitation (**"Turn your gift into a video they'll love"** + a clean **"Free · Takes a minute · No app needed"**) is now the first and biggest thing on screen.
- The code reassurance is kept but shrunk to one calm line - **"Your 30% off code is on its way to {email}"** - so nobody loses the confirmation or the address.
- The "check your spam folder" line and the "While you wait..." label are removed from this screen. (The spam reminder still appears later on the "Check your email" screen, where it's actually useful.)

Nothing about the offer, the email step, the discount, or how the video is delivered changed - the email is captured earlier on the claim page, the code is still emailed by Klaviyo, and the video is still emailed. See the attached BEFORE/AFTER phone screenshots.

## Where this sits and why

The one goal is more honest Amazon reviews. Of the last 30 days of review clicks, **17 of 19 (89%)** come from the thank-you screen that only appears *after* someone finishes a video; the emailed review reminders produced **0**. So the screen that decides whether a warm visitor starts a video is the most direct lever we have on reviews - and it's under-worked (last touched 2026-06-16).

Ranked leaks this cycle:
1. **In-app entry (this change).** Warmest visitors arrive already having given their email, yet only ~31% (28 of 90) reach the create step, and ~37% of the warmest (claim-forwarded) visitors never even pick a role. Session replay shows most of these leave within ~6 seconds without a single tap - a decision made the instant the screen paints. Highest *value* leak because it gates the 89% review engine.
2. **Claim page email capture.** Bigger by raw headcount (~58% never give an email) but flat and recently worked twice; the emails it captures feed a reminder path that produced 0 of 19 review clicks in 30 days - low review value per recovered visitor.
3. **Preview/share review asks.** Real traffic, ~0 review clicks; already reworked once in June to no effect.

## Verdict on the last change (with the statistics)

The two 2026-07-23 claim-page changes (warmer opening voice + surfacing the crochet-character portrait) were both shipped **unmeasurable by design**. Reading them now: the claim page captured **41.9% (57 of 136)** this window vs **39.8% (66 of 166)** before - a **+2.2 point** move that is **NOT statistically significant** (`node tools/significance.mjs 66 166 57 136` -> p=0.705; at this traffic only a ~16-point swing could be told from luck). Two honesty caveats: this window mixes ~5 pre-change days with ~9 post-change days, and page views fell 166->136. **So this is neither a win nor a loss - it stays pending**, and cannot be called a win without a significant result. It becomes cleanly comparable around 2026-08-05.

## What the independent auditor said, and how I responded

The auditor **approved** the plan, re-ran every reproducible number to an exact match, and left two *minor* notes:
- *The cause (the code-status block repels people) is a bet the data can't confirm, and one slice even leans the other way (claim visitors pick a role 63% vs 44% for non-claim, though that gap is itself not significant, p=0.071).* I kept the auditor's required commitment: shipped as **not measurable**, and I will not claim it worked without a significant test. If it later reads flat, the honest interpretation is "some visitors simply never wanted the video," not "the copy failed." The reason this is still worth shipping is that the fix is one-directional: removing a "go check your email" instruction and leading with the invitation cannot *lower* the number - so even a wrong guess about the cause can't make it worse.
- *The prize is tiny and can never be proven at this traffic (~1-2 extra review clicks a fortnight).* True, and I've labelled it exactly that - a small, compounding bet, not a measurable experiment.

## How I verified it

Booted the app and loaded the real edited welcome screen (HTTP 200); confirmed the invitation now leads, the slim one-line code confirmation with the email address is present, and the old green banner, the "check your spam" line, and "While you wait..." are gone from this screen while the spam note still appears on the final "Check your email" screen. Rendered mobile BEFORE (live site) and AFTER (this build) full-page screenshots - attached. No test data was written to our event log (confirmed 0 rows).

## What to re-measure, and when

Around **2026-08-15** (needs ~2 weeks of visitors after today, both windows on/after 2026-08-01): the in-app steps (arrived -> picked a role -> pressed Create -> started a video), split by whether the visitor came from the claim page, then run the significance test. **Any swing under ~13-20 points will be invisible at this volume**, so the most likely honest outcome is "can't tell" - that's expected and fine. It will only ever be called a win if the significance test says so.
telegram_summary: Last change (07-23 claim-page voice + portrait): email capture 41.9% (57/136) vs 39.8% (66/166) - NOT significant (p=0.705), stays pending, no win/loss. Top leak: the welcome screen after people land in the create app - warmest visitors, ~37% leave within seconds before picking a role, and it gates the thank-you page behind 89% of all review clicks. What I did: for visitors from the claim page, made the 'make a video' invitation the big first thing, and shrank the 'your code is on its way' notice to one calm line - dropping the 'check your spam' nudge and 'While you wait...' that pointed people back to their inbox. Small reversible bet, too small to prove here. Before/after photos attached.
